GreedySolver final class

The package's solver: maps a Region plus a list of constraints to a list of sub-regions, ratatui-inspired but greedy rather than linear-programming (the retired simplex prototype never converged — see CassowarySolver).

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly bool $roundSplit = false, public readonly bool $remainderToLast = false, public readonly bool $truncateOverflow = true, public readonly int $minShare = 0, public readonly int $reserveGap = 0, public readonly int $reserveLead = 0)
static new(): selfDefault factory — matches LayoutSolver convention.
static greedy(): self
static compat(): selfsugar-panels parity mode: round-split + remainder-to-last + non-truncating overflow. Opt-in seam for retiring sugar-panels's duplicated distribute() /distributeFlex() without regressing its goldens.
withRoundSplit(bool $on = true): selfRound Percentage/Ratio proportional sizes with round() instead of floor().
withRemainderToLast(bool $on = true): selfHand the rounding remainder to the LAST region (or LAST Fill/Max) instead of the first.
withoutOverflowTruncation(): selfKeep each region at its full base size on overflow (layout runs off-grid) instead of truncating proportionally.
withOverflowTruncation(bool $on = true): selfRe-enable (or disable) proportional overflow truncation.
withMinShare(int $cells = 1, int $reserveGap = 0, int $reserveLead = 0): selfEngage the sequential min-share floor: split the region proportionally across its Fill weights while reserving at least $cells cell(s) for every region NOT yet placed, so the trailing region never collapses to 0 in a tight viewport. This is the opt-in seam that lets sugar-panels retire its hand-rolled NON-flex distribute() with byte parity — the fourth quirk compat()'s three flags cannot express.
static minShareFloor(int $cells = 1, int $reserveGap = 0, int $reserveLead = 0): selfDedicated construction door for the sequential min-share floor: the compat knobs arrive at the mode's truth (floor split, remainder-to-last; truncateOverflow neutral-true) instead of inheriting a policy the floor path ignores — the loud alternative to withMinShare()'s reset when the instance is being built, not retuned.
solve(Region $region, Direction $dir, array $constraints): arrayInstance solve — satisfies LayoutSolver.
static solveStatic(Region $area, Direction $dir, array $constraints): arrayStatic convenience for the default (floor / remainder-first / truncating) behaviour — reachable without holding an instance.
demandOf(Region $area, Direction $dir, array $constraints): intThe integer APPETITE of a constraint set against the frame's solved axis — the README's documented host-side degradation comparison, mechanized: Length at its exact size, Percentage/Ratio resolved against the span under this instance's rounding policy, Min at its floor, Max at its cap, and Fill at 0 (it claims only slack, so it is never left "unmet"). Demand above the span means the set cannot be satisfied whole: either the proportional truncation fires (fixed + Min floors already exceed the axis) or a slack consumer is served below its appetite. Which pane lost what stays a per-frame question one integer cannot split — see the README Degradation section, which still recommends withoutOverflowTruncation() when collapse must be visible per region. Same boundary refusals as solve(); the walk is pure integer arithmetic (carve-out 4 applies to its products too).

SugarCraft\Constraints\Constraint

Constraint abstract class

Abstract base class for all constraint types used by LayoutSolver::solve().

MethodSummary
static length(int $n): LengthFixed character-cell count.
static min(int $n): MinAt least $n cells — a soft floor. Takes slack directly only when the set has neither Fill nor Max; otherwise grows only from cells a Max clamp hands back, which Min takes before Fill. Does not guarantee $n when demand exceeds the area.
static fill(int $weight = 1): FillFills all remaining space; $weight controls proportional distribution when multiple Fill constraints compete.
static percentage(int $n): PercentageProportional size as a percentage (0-100) of the available area.
static ratio(int $numerator, int $denominator): RatioProportional size based on a ratio (numerator / denominator).
static max(int $n): MaxUpper-bound size cap; takes slack greedily (proportional to its cap among the slack consumers) but never more than $n. The clamp pass can also give cells BACK from this type when the greedy share rode over the cap — the hand-back rides Min first, then Fill, and reaches Length/Percentage/Ratio only in a set with neither.

SugarCraft\Constraints\Dock

DockGeometry final readonly class

Immutable result of DockLayout::resolve() — concrete grid regions for one frame.

MethodSummary
static new(array $regions = [], array $dividerColumns = []): selfThe validating public door for untrusted payloads: every element of the shape is checked before construction (the scan used to live in the private constructor, where resolve() paid it once per frame on bytes it had just built itself — finding 028 moved it to this door; the paint path takes solved() instead).
regionFor(string $paneId): ?RegionThe region assigned to a pane, or null when the pane is absent from this geometry. Absent covers three distinct states — the pane was never docked, its side was dropped by the degradation ladder, or the frame was degenerate. A null alone does not say which; hosts that must distinguish a dropped side from an undocked pane compare against the input DockLayout (its slots()/columnShare() still describe intent). Note a 0-width region is NOT null: an active side planned at 0 columns keeps a width-0 region by design (see the DockLayout class notes).
dividerColumns(): array
isEmpty(): boolTrue when the frame was degenerate (non-positive width/height) and the layout resolved to nothing.

DockLayout final class

Immutable dock/pane-layout description: a center surface flanked by two optional vertical stacks of docked panes, resolved into concrete DockGeometry for any Region frame.

MethodSummary
static new(string $centerPaneId = 'center'): selfEmpty dock: center pane id defaults to the neutral 'center' (2026-11: was 'chat', but the factory should not bake one app's vocabulary — candy-code passes its 'chat' explicitly at every call site), no side slots, both column shares at the 1/3 design default, center minimum 24 cols, side minimum 20 cols, 1-col dividers.
withSlotAdded(Side $side, string $paneId, ?int $index = null): selfDock a pane onto a side. Null index appends; index is an insertion position in 0..count. Duplicate pane ids across BOTH sides are refused, and so is the center pane's own id — a pane has exactly one home.
withSlotRemoved(string $paneId): selfUndock a pane from whichever side holds it. Unknown pane ids are a no-op returning the identical instance — the deliberate counterpart to withSlotMovedTo(), which THROWS on an unknown id: removals run in idempotent teardown paths where "already gone" is success, while a move of a never-docked pane can only be a caller bug. The README's Dock walkthrough names this asymmetry so hosts do not have to read both docblocks to find it.
withSlotMovedTo(string $paneId, Side $side, ?int $index = null): selfMove a pane across sides or reorder it within its side. Null index moves to the end of the destination stack. Unknown pane ids throw — a move of a pane that was never docked is a caller bug, not a no-op (the idempotent no-op side of this asymmetry is withSlotRemoved()).
withColumnShare(Side $side, int $num, int $denom): selfSet a side's column share. Invalid rationals throw; the pair rule leftShare + rightShare <= 1/2 is enforced by CLAMPING the requested share (never throwing) — the center is the primary surface and must keep at least half the usable columns once the host starts tightening shares. The creation default (thirds) predates any tightening and is documented on the class.
withColumnShareExact(Side $side, int $num, int $denom): selfStrict sibling of withColumnShare(): identical validation and the identical pair rule, but a share that WOULD be clamped is refused with \InvalidArgumentException naming the request and the ceiling, never silently tightened — for hosts that treat "asked for what the rule cannot grant" as a caller bug.
withStackWeight(Side $side, int $index, int $num, int $denom): selfReplace the rational stack weight at $index (a current position in the side's stack, 0..count-1).
withStackWeightFor(Side $side, string $paneId, int $num, int $denom): selfId-keyed sibling of withStackWeight(): the slot is found by pane id, so a removal that shifted the stack since the caller last looked can never make a positional index weight the wrong pane. An id that is not docked on $side throws, naming the miss.
withFixedColumns(Side $side, int $cols): selfClaim EXACTLY $cols columns for a side, bypassing the share pass — "20 columns, always" is what the share-only surface could not express. $cols = 0 returns the side to share-driven planning (the default). The center's floor ladder still applies to the remaining pool: a fixed side that starves the center below centerMinCols is dropped by the same degradation ladder that removes share-driven sides, and — by design — the min-protection RAISE never touches a fixed side, since a raise would undo the exactness the caller declared.
withMinimums(int $centerMinCols, int $sideMinCols): selfSet the column minimums; both must be >= 1.
slots(Side $side): array
columnShare(Side $side): array
resolve(Region $frame): DockGeometryLay this dock out inside $frame.
toArray(): arrayExact versioned manifest shape.
static fromArray(array $data): selfParse a manifest produced by toArray(). Strict at the boundary — every failure throws InvalidArgumentException naming the offending key path, including a slot id that collides with the center pane (a pane has exactly one home). Hand-edited data that violates basic ranges is REFUSED here (fail-fast), while the 1/2 pair rule stays a withColumnShare() clamping policy: restored manifests keep their persisted shares untouched (the thirds default included), so round-trip identity holds.
